cheng: FYI I ran the alpha on a long-context smoke (16k->64k step-up). Seeing divergence starting ~32k tokens when KV rebase occurs.
zoe: ugh. is it regression vs float16 baseline or new int8 only?
cheng: appears in int8 path (quantized weights + int8 attention kernels). float16 doesn't diverge on same trace.
liam: can you paste the minimal repro?
cheng: repro script below — deterministic seed, same prompt, same sampling.
cheng: ```bash
# repro.sh
python run_infer.py --model orpheus-alpha-int8 --context 65536 --prompt-file tests/long_prompt.txt --seed 42 --no-stream > out.txt
```
maria: what does the diff look like? small token shift or full collapse?
cheng: token-level drift starts as small prob differences at ~32k then autocorrects a few times then eventually produces semantically different continuation at ~37k. patched log snippet: 
cheng: ```
[32012] p(next="the")=0.072 vs baseline 0.081
[32055] p(next="to")=0.001 vs baseline 0.045
[37210] continuation diverged (baseline: "...and he left." alpha-int8: "...but suddenly the")
```
sam: that smells like RoPE scaling mismatch or cache index slip when we downcast. Did you see any off-by-one in KV indices?
cheng: KV indices look continuous in our debug dump, but the rotary phase multipliers in quantized kernels are different by tiny eps. suspect accumulation error in quantized sin/cos table.
zoe: could be quant table resolution or different interpolation. we saw a similar symptom in a 12k bring-up last quarter.
liam: run exact-fp shadow: run the same kernel path with float32 shim to compare internal kv keys and rotary application.
maria: how are we measuring divergence? KL, token mismatch rate, or LM-score?
cheng: tracking three metrics: token mismatch rate (TMR), prefix BLEU, and LM-log-loss delta. Current: int8 TMR @ 40k=0.34% vs baseline 0.01%. LM loss delta ~+0.12.
sam: 0.34% seems small but for long-context that compounds. do we have a histogram of where mismatches cluster?
cheng: yes: 60% of mismatches occur in 32k-40k window. tail after 50k is mostly stable once drift happens.
zoe: action items?
liam: 1) run fp32 shadow as mentioned, 2) rerun int8 with higher-precision sin/cos table (double prec precompute), 3) check block boundary KV copy routine for stride alignment.
maria: can we do a quick canary to prod-ish to verify throughput effect? deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: canary/orpheus-alpha-int8 -> 3 pods in dedicated-staging at 15:12 UTC.
sam: also please capture kv-checksum at each prefix checkpoint and prod/alpha diffs. Add header: KV_CHECKSUM:<step>:<crc32>.
cheng: added checksum dump to repro. sample: KV_CHECKSUM:32000:0x9f4a12c3 vs baseline 0x9f4a12c3 (match), KV_CHECKSUM:32768:0x1a2b3c4d vs baseline 0x1a2b3c4e (off by 1)
zoe: off-by-one in checksum suggests tiny bit flip or rounding change in one element. that aligns w/ rotary table rounding hypothesis.
liam: try running int8 with RK=rotary_kv_scale * (1 + 1e-6) to see sensitivity. small epsilon may reveal linear response.
maria: can we repro on cpu-only to eliminate kernel kernel scheduling/packing bug?
cheng: repro successful on cpu with int8-emulation (same drift). downcasts reproduce issue, so not purely packing.
sam: next: re-run quant pipeline with increased quantization bit-width for rotary table (e.g., 10-bit instead of 8) and re-evaluate.
zoe: timeline? If we can get an fp32 shadow and quant-table tweak today, we can validate by EOD. who owns the bench runs?
liam: I can run shadow + small param sweep (eps +/- [1e-7,1e-6,1e-5]) and KV-checksum comparison. estimate 3 hours on the bench cluster.
maria: i'll prepare the PR to enable higher-precision precompute flag in quant pipeline and a test that asserts checksum stability up to 64k.
cheng: i'll collect all diffs and produce a short triage doc with sample traces and metric plots.
liam: if epsilon sensitivity shows linear effects, we can ship a quick mitigation: shadow rotate tables in int8 path using float16 intermediates.
sam: long-term we might need a quant-aware rotary encode that preserves phase at long-range. open an RFC if we need design time.
zoe: thanks all. please post the benchmark links when done.
cheng: uploaded artifacts to s3: s3://redwood-ci/eng-ml/5387654321/ — includes out.txt, kv-dumps, checksums, diffs.
liam: starting runs now. will update with results.
cheng: thanks — ping me if you need more traces. :thumbsup:
